title: Melissa Meredith (CEO of a public benefit corporation) sets the book against the NYT business-school argument — 'value creation vs. value captured'
summary: Meredith co-founded and runs Collective Kairos, a public benefit corporation. She posted Christopher Marquis's New York Times finding that firms appointing business-educated CEOs saw wages and labor's share fall while shareholder value rose about 5%, with output, investment and employment flat, and lined his case up beside Eric's. Her own framing is extraction against regeneration, with the public benefit corporation as a structure already available and the book as where to start.
blockquote: Eric Ries called for the end of the shareholder primacy era for nearly the same reason that Christopher called for the end of business schools - value creation vs. value captured.
attribution_title: CEO & Co-Founder, Collective Kairos (a public benefit corporation)
